THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.
Heard on admission.

2. Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted his arguments that Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation, to the death of 2 years old child, which is exorbitant and sought for allowing this appeal.

3. As against this, Sri.Veeranagouda Malipatil, learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has submitted his arguments that Tribunal has passed the just and proper compensation and that there are no grounds to interfere with the judgment passed by the Tribunal.

To substantiate his arguments, he has relied upon the decision in the case of MEENA DEVI vs. NUNU CHAND MAHTO @ NEMCHAND MAHTO reported in AIR 2022 SC 5006.
4.

entities.text: MEENA DEVI vs. NUNU CHAND MAHTO @ NEMCHAND MAHTO reported in AIR 2022 SC 5006
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have gone through the judgment relied upon by the leaned counsel for the respondent No.1.

At paragraphs 10 and 11 of the said judgment it is observed as under:
"10.

Thus relying upon the observation, it is said that in place of issuing any guidelines for determination of compensation in case of death of a child, it may be left open to be decided in the facts and circumstances of each case.

In the case of M.S.
Grewal (supra), 14 school students died due to drowning in a river.
This Court noticing that the students were belonging to upper middle class background, however awarded the compensation to the tune of Rs. 5,00,000/-.

Thereafter in the case of Kishan Gopal (supra), a child aged about 10 years died in a road accident took place on 19.7.1992, this Court made departure from the IInd Schedule of M.V. Act and accepted the notional income of Rs. 30,000 in place of Rs. 15,000/- applying the analogy that the value of rupee has come down drastically since 1994 when the notional income of Rs. 15000/- was fixed in IInd Schedule of the MV Act.

However accepting the notional income as Rs. 30,000/- and as per the age of the parents i.e.
36 years, the loss of dependency was calculated applying the multiplier of 15 at Rs.
4,50,000/- and a sum of Rs. 50,000/- was awarded under conventional heads awarding a total sum of compensation of Rs. 5.00.000/-
11.

Recently in the case of Kurvan Ansari @ Kurvan Ali and another v. Shyam Kishore Murmu and another (2022) 1 SCC 317: (AIR 2021 SC (Supp) 1), wherein a child aged about 7 years died in a road accident took place on 6.9.2004, this Court taking notional income as Rs. 25,000/-, applying the multiplier of 15, calculated the loss of dependency as Rs. 3.75.000/- and adding Rs.

2 55,000/- in conventional heads, awarded Rs.4.70,000/-."
5.

entities.text: Divisional Manager vs Smt. Rabiya Begum And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In paragraphs 14 and 15 the Tribunal has observed as under:
"14.

At this stage, it is necessary to clarify that as per the decision of a Three-Judge Bench of this Court in Nagappa v. Gurdayal Singh and others (2003) 2 SCC 274: (AIR 2003 SC 674), it was observed that under the MV Act, there is no restriction that the Tribunal/Court cannot award compensation exceeding the amount so claimed.

entities.text: Nagappa v. Gurdayal Singh and others (2003) 2 SCC 274: (AIR 2003 SC 674)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal/Court ought to award 'just' compensation which is reasonable in the facts relying upon the evidence produced on record.
Therefore, less valuation, if any, made in the Claim Petition would not be impediment to award just compensation exceeding the claimed amount.
15. Accordingly, this appeal is allowed.
The amount of compensation, as awarded by the High Court is enhanced by Rs. 3,00,000/-, in addition.

The total amount of compensation would be Rs.
5,00,000/-.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest @ 7% p.a. from the date of Claim Petition till realization.
United India Insurance Company within a period of four weeks from today.
16. The parties to bear their own costs."

6. Considering the facts and circumstances of this case and keeping in mind the decision relied upon by the learned counsel for the respondent No.1, it is held that there are no grounds to interfere with the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
Hence, appeal is dismissed.

Sd/-
